page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression tests, both scoring in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also demonstrate average tier performance, with uncached read speeds reaching 108.04 GB/sec and write speeds at 47.67 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6.8xlarge offers a standard resource density for general-purpose workloads, balancing a high vCPU count with moderate memory capacity without the added cost of bundled local SSDs or GPU accelerators. The lack of local storage requires external block storage, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads. Given the average multi-core and database benchmark results, this instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, redis caching, and general-purpose enterprise applications that do not demand extreme single-thread processing speeds.
